# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Deaf monkey - I can see the bomb but can't hear or speak in a way anyone but Mute and Blind can perceive (Mute reads gestures, Blind reaches but can't see/hear). I need to communicate what I see using speech (heard by Mute and Blind) and gestures (seen by Mute only).

Let me record what I see: Display shows 0, light is yellow, and there are 5 wires with colors: 1-green, 2-white, 3-red, 4-yellow, 5-blue.

Since this is the first turn and I haven't received anything yet (Blind and Mute haven't acted or their messages haven't arrived), I should share my observations now via speech so Blind can hear it directly, and Mute can also hear it. This is efficient since both can receive my speech.

I'll describe the display, light, and wire colors clearly and wait for Mute to tell me (via speech, since only I can hear... wait, I cannot hear anything). Actually Mute cannot speak at all - only gesture. So Mute's information must reach me via gesture, which I can see.

Let me speak my findings so Blind and Mute both get it now.

```
speak(text="Display reads 0. Light is yellow. Wires left to right: 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 ☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute gestured to me: 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ - this looks like "point" followed by three "up/one" symbols. This could mean "wire number 3" or "point to wire 3" (👉 = pointing, ☝ = index finger up, possibly indicating counting or a specific number).

Since Mute can read the manual, they might be telling me which wire to focus on, or asking me to confirm something about wire 3, or indicating "wire 3" as in "look at position 3" (three ☝ symbols could mean the number 3, or repeated emphasis).

I don't have enough context yet since Mute cannot speak, only gesture, and I already told them what I see. This gesture might be Mute's way of indicating "wire 3" is important (perhaps the manual says to cut wire 3, or asks about wire 3's color).

I already stated wire 3 is red. Let me confirm this back to Mute and Blind, and wait for more gestures to clarify the plan.

```
speak(text="Confirming: wire 3 is red. Display 0, light yellow. Waiting for further instruction from Mute.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute added a 👍 (thumbs up) before the same gesture sequence: 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝. The thumbs up likely confirms my previous statement was correct - that wire 3 is indeed the one they mean, and it's red as I confirmed. This is Mute acknowledging "yes, wire 3" is the target.

This suggests the manual says wire 3 (red) should be cut, or is significant in some way. Since Mute can't speak, they're confirming via gesture that wire 3 is correct/important.

I should relay this confirmation to Blind, since Blind needs to act but can't perceive gestures or colors. Let me speak to Blind directly, telling them wire 3 (red) seems to be the target based on Mute's confirmation.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has confirmed wire 3, which is red, seems to be the important one. Waiting for Mute to clarify the action needed - cut, or something else.")
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, wire 3 red confirmed. What should Blind do with it - cut it, or something else? Gesture if you can indicate an action.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gave a simple thumbs up 👍 - this confirms my understanding that wire 3 (red) is correct. But this doesn't tell me the specific action needed (cut, hold, connect, etc.).

Since Mute can't speak and can only gesture to me, and I already asked for an action clarification, this thumbs up might just be a general "yes, correct" without more detail. I need to think about how Mute could convey more complex actions with limited gesture vocabulary.

Perhaps Mute is confirming that cutting is the correct action (the default assumption), or simply confirming identification of the wire, leaving the actual action instruction to reach Blind through Mute's gestures to me, which I then relay in speech to Blind.

Given the constraints, I should pass this confirmation to Blind and suggest that cutting wire 3 (red) seems to be the safest interpretation unless Mute gestures otherwise. But since a wrong action is fatal, I should push Mute for more specific gesture-based confirmation on the action itself.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Got your thumbs up on wire 3, red. Confirming target wire only. Do you want Blind to cut it? Please gesture a specific action - for example thumbs up again for cut, or a different gesture for another action like hold or disconnect.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]

Mute gave two thumbs up 👍 👍 - this seems to confirm "yes, cut it" as I proposed (thumbs up again for cut). This is likely Mute's affirmative response to my specific question about cutting wire 3.

Given the turn order is Blind, Mute, Deaf - Blind acts first each round, then Mute, then me. This means Blind has already acted or will act before receiving my current message, and won't get this info until next round unless I speak now for the next round's Blind turn.

I need to relay this to Blind: cut wire 3 (red). Since speech reaches Blind (they can hear), this should get through.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed by Mute: cut wire 3, which is red.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb has changed successfully - wire 3 was cut correctly and the light changed from yellow to green (good sign - progress!). Now the state is:
- Display: 0
- Light: green
- Wires: 1-white, 2-yellow, 3-CUT, 4-blue, 5-green

I need to report this new state to Mute so they can check the manual for the next step. Let me describe the current board clearly.

```
speak(text="Success! Wire 3 was cut correctly, bomb changed. New state: Display 0, light now green. Wires: 1 white, 2 yellow, 3 CUT, 4 blue, 5 green.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]

Mute sent two gestures this turn:
1. 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ - pointing with five ☝ symbols, likely indicating wire 5
2. 👍 👍 - two thumbs up, which previously meant "cut it"

So Mute is indicating wire 5 (green) should be cut, following the same pattern as before (point + count = wire number, thumbs up = confirm, double thumbs up = cut action).

Let me confirm this interpretation and relay to Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood: wire 5, green, cut it. Confirming before I relay to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute says: cut wire 5, which is green.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Another success! Wire 5 was cut correctly. New state:
- Display: 0
- Light: white
- Wires: 1-yellow, 2-blue, 3-CUT, 4-white, 5-CUT

Let me report this to Mute so they can determine the next step.

```
speak(text="Success again! Wire 5 cut correctly. New state: Display 0, light now white. Wires: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 CUT, 4 white, 5 CUT.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]

Mute is indicating wire 1 (👉 ☝ = point + one) and confirming with 👍👍 (cut action). Following the established pattern, this means "cut wire 1".

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood: wire 1, yellow, cut it. Relaying to Blind now.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute says: cut wire 1, which is yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Another successful cut! Wire 1 was cut correctly. New state:
- Display: 0
- Light: red
- Wires: 1-CUT, 2-white, 3-CUT, 4-blue, 5-CUT

Only wires 2 and 4 remain uncut. Let me report this new state to Mute.

```
speak(text="Success! Wire 1 cut correctly. New state: Display 0, light now red. Wires: 1 CUT, 2 white, 3 CUT, 4 blue, 5 CUT. Only wires 2 and 4 remain.")
wait()
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]

Mute is indicating wire 4 (👉 + four ☝) and confirming cut action (👍👍). This means "cut wire 4, which is blue".

The light being red is concerning - light being red could mean caution/danger, but since Mute has access to the manual and is confirming this action deliberately, I'll trust their judgment based on the manual's instructions.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood: wire 4, blue, cut it. Relaying to Blind now.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute says: cut wire 4, which is blue.")
wait()
```
